output.query: psychogenic nonepileptic seizures coexisting with epilepsy diagnosis and treatment

results.finding: Diagnostic levels for PNES: documented PNES requires a typical event recorded on video-EEG without epileptiform activity before, during or after it, together with a history consistent with PNES; lower levels rely on witnessed or video-recorded events without EEG. Epilepsy and PNES can coexist, and each must be documented separately.
results.source: LaFrance WC et al., Epilepsia 2013;54:2005-2018 | Minimum requirements for the diagnosis of psychogenic nonepileptic seizures: a staged approach

results.finding: In adults with dissociative seizures, cognitive behavioral therapy added to standardized medical care did not reduce monthly seizure frequency at 12 months but improved several secondary outcomes, including seizure bothersomeness, longest seizure-free period and psychosocial functioning.
results.source: Goldstein LH et al., Lancet Psychiatry 2020;7:491-505 | Cognitive behavioural therapy for adults with dissociative seizures (CODES)

output.summary: Video-EEG capture of a typical event without an EEG correlate documents PNES (LaFrance 2013), and PNES may coexist with epilepsy. CBT added to specialist care improved secondary outcomes in the CODES trial (Goldstein 2020).

Continue lamotrigine 200 mg twice daily unchanged for the controlled epilepsy.
Refer for CBT-based psychotherapy with psychiatry, addressing the precipitant (her daughter's diagnosis and her guilt) and the childhood trauma history.
Taper alprazolam gradually with addiction-medicine input, given the escalating use and the seizure risk of abrupt withdrawal.

Video-EEG recorded seven habitual events without any EEG change before, during or after them, with the known right anterior temporal interictal sharp waves unchanged: documented PNES coexisting with epilepsy (LaFrance 2013).

PNES and epilepsy coexist in a substantial minority of patients; escalating antiseizure medicine for PNES adds toxicity without benefit.

general.query: focal epilepsy in adults: definition, classification, imaging and first-line treatment

results.finding: Epilepsy is present after at least two unprovoked seizures more than 24 hours apart, after one unprovoked seizure with a recurrence risk of at least 60% over the next 10 years, or when an epilepsy syndrome is diagnosed.
results.source: Fisher RS et al., Epilepsia 2014;55:475-482 | ILAE official report: a practical clinical definition of epilepsy

results.finding: Seizures are classified by onset as focal, generalized or unknown; focal seizures are described by awareness and by their first motor or non-motor feature, and may evolve to focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures.
results.source: Fisher RS et al., Epilepsia 2017;58:522-530 | Operational classification of seizure types by the International League Against Epilepsy: position paper of the ILAE Commission for Classification and Terminology

results.finding: A harmonized epilepsy MRI protocol (3D T1 and 3D FLAIR at about 1 mm isotropic resolution and high-resolution coronal T2) is recommended for adults with focal epilepsy; non-dedicated protocols miss subtle lesions.
results.source: Bernasconi A et al., Epilepsia 2019;60:1054-1068 | Recommendations for the use of structural magnetic resonance imaging in the care of patients with epilepsy: a consensus report from the International League Against Epilepsy Neuroimaging Task Force

results.finding: Lamotrigine or levetiracetam is offered as first-line monotherapy for focal seizures, with carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, zonisamide or lacosamide as further options.
results.source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, NG217 2022 | Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

results.finding: Drug-resistant epilepsy is failure of adequate trials of two tolerated, appropriately chosen and used antiseizure medication schedules to achieve sustained seizure freedom.
results.source: Kwan P et al., Epilepsia 2010;51:1069-1077 | Definition of drug resistant epilepsy: consensus proposal by the ad hoc Task Force of the ILAE Commission on Therapeutic Strategies

general.summary: Epilepsy is diagnosed after two unprovoked seizures more than 24 hours apart or one with a high recurrence risk, and focal seizures are classified by onset and awareness (ILAE 2014, 2017). A dedicated epilepsy-protocol MRI is the imaging of choice (ILAE 2019). Lamotrigine or levetiracetam is first-line monotherapy for focal seizures (NICE NG217), and drug resistance is failure of two appropriate medication schedules (ILAE 2010).

She has been to the emergency department 4 times in the past 2 months for these events. However, the semiology of the new events differs significantly from her prior documented epileptic seizures: (1) longer duration — the new events last 5-20 minutes (prior seizures lasted 1-2 minutes), (2) eyes closed during events (prior seizures had eyes open with staring), (3) wild bilateral thrashing with side-to-side head movement (prior seizures had behavioral arrest with oral automatisms — lip smacking and chewing), (4) preserved awareness during some events — she reports remembering everything during the episode, (5) no post-ictal confusion (prior seizures always had 20-30 minutes of post-ictal confusion and word-finding difficulty). The precipitant: 3 months ago, her 16-year-old daughter was diagnosed with epilepsy, causing severe maternal guilt and anxiety. She has been taking increasing amounts of alprazolam.
